title: Sandmen and the coming of Christianity
summary: How the Sandmen turned toward the Underworld.

claims.text: Dreamcrafters of old cultures had worked their way into religious roles, mostly aimed at the living, who still believed in old spirits and gods.

When Christianity spread, many newer Sandmen looked to their place among the dead instead, believing the living to be in God's keeping; saints, priests and prophets no longer wished to hear tales of the Underworld.
Worry that great secrets might be lost to Oblivion through Shadow-ridden Dreamcrafters gave them the shared purpose that later formed the Guild.
Fewer Sandmen serve the Hierarchy than the Heretics, Renegades or Vagabonds; many who practice Phantasm see Transcendence as close kin to dreaming, which puts them at odds with Hierarchy teaching.
Those in Hierarchy Circles often work as state-backed artists or as spies and infiltrators.
Many Sandmen once filled Heretical Mystery and Sensualist cults; the Succubus Randi Trate is famed for bringing four dream-infants of one mortal into the Shadowlands at once.
